label: sec:surreal-appendix-conclusion
title: Open questions and outlook
html:
The surreal-number lift of QOU raises several questions:

  1. Mathlib gap. There is no mature surreal-analysis library in mathlib. Formalising the birthday-grading definition and the Hoefsmit-as-\{L\mid R\} proposition rigorously requires completing the surreal-numbers development in mathlib (the SetTheory.Game.Basic hierarchy) up to a real-closed-field witness.
  2. Surreal measure? The category \mathbf{No} carries no canonical Lebesgue measure. Loeb-type constructions on hyperfinite subsets of \mathbf{No} yield finitely additive measures that pull back to \mathbb{R} under the standard part. We leave open whether such a construction recovers the Frobenius integral \int_A up to an infinitesimal.
  3. Surreal Hilbert-like object. The scattering pipeline's Hilbert space \mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{phys}} lacks a surreal analogue with a canonical inner product. We should investigate whether a birthday-bounded completion yields a weaker surrogate—sufficient for the mass formula but lacking spectral theory.
  4. Categorical size. Since \mathbf{No} is a proper class, defining \mathbf{Mod}_{\mathbf{No}} or \mathbf{Rep}_{\mathbf{No}}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2)) requires universe-polymorphic foundations or restriction to a set-sized Hahn-series sub-field. We sidestep this by stating axioms over a fixed real-closed field K extending \mathbb{R}.
  5. Genuine generalisations. The strict QOU axioms (\int \circ \eta = \mathrm{id}, \mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0) might force the \varepsilon-relaxed versions to coincide with the strict ones in any rigid monoidal category. If so, the \varepsilon-flexibility is illusory. We conjecture the flexibility is genuine when the ground ring is not a field (infinitesimal Frobenius), but we lack a proof or counterexample.
  6. Kashaev as a surreal statement. The reformulation \mathrm{st}\bigl(2 \pi \log |J_K(q_\omega, \omega)|/\omega\bigr) = \mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K) (Kashaev surreal) is equivalent to the classical conjecture, modulo the meaning of q_\omega. It separates the algebraic (Hecke/Markov) content from the transcendental (dilogarithm, hyperbolic volume) content.

Accomplishments of this appendix:

  • We provide an explicit ambient for the q \to 1 limit and renormalisation blow-ups, avoiding informal \infty notation.
  • We exhibit an isomorphism between the Hoefsmit seminormal form (central to the mass formula) and Conway's \{L \mid R\} construction.
  • We establish a disciplined framework for \varepsilon-relaxed axioms.
  • We catalogue which QOU constructions are purely algebraic (hence field-polymorphic) versus genuinely analytic.

This appendix serves as raw material for future work rather than a completed extension of the theory.
